summary: Julius Euting was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen and under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as a librarian in Tübingen and as Director of the National and University Library, Strasbourg (1871; 1900–1909).

Julius Grill was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the universities of Tübingen and Jena, as well as under Adalbert Kuhn and Rudolf von Roth. He served as Professor of Old Testament Exegesis at Tübingen from 1888 to 1913.

Julius Hoffory was a linguist who studied at the universities of Copenhagen, Strasbourg, and Berlin. He held an academic post at the University of Berlin from circa 1883 to 1897 and taught Josef Schick.

Julius Jolly was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin, Leipzig, Munich (PhD), and Würzburg under Albrecht Weber and Martin Haug. He served as professor at Würzburg (1877–1920) and Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta (1882–1883).

Julius Lipner, a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, studied at Jadavpur, Jnana Deepa, and King's College London under Hywel David Lewis. He taught at the University of Birmingham before serving as Professor of Hinduism at Cambridge (1975–2013).

Julius Mohl was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Sinology. He studied at Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy, Abel-Rémusat, and Eugène Burnouf, later serving as professor at Tübingen (1826–1834) and Collège de France (1847–1876).

Julius Pokorny was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna under Rudolf Much. He held posts at the universities of Vienna (ca. 1913–1920), Berlin (ca. 1920–1935), Bern, Zurich (ca. 1944–1970), and Munich (ca. 1955–1970).

Julius Schubring was a scholar in history and archaeology. He pursued his university studies at the University of Göttingen (ca. 1857–1858), the University of Bonn (ca. 1858–1860), and Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (ca. 1860–1862).

Julius Zupitza was a linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Moriz Haupt. He held academic posts at the University of Breslau (ca. 1869–1872), University of Vienna (ca. 1872–1876), and University of Berlin (ca. 1876–1895).
Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a doctoral degree in literature at the University of Tokyo. He served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University from circa 2009 to 2013.

Jun Takashima is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara. He served as associate professor at Aichi Prefectural University (ca. 1990–1994) and professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies in 2020.

Jundo Nagashima is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned a PhD from the University of Bristol under Paul Williams and studied under Alexis Sanderson and Seitatsu Matsunami, later serving as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2013–2017).

June McDaniel is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned an MTS at Emory University and a PhD at the University of Chicago. She served as Professor of the History of Religions at the College of Charleston (attested 2000, 2015).

Junglan Bang is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Dongguk University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg in 2012 under Harunaga Isaacson, later working as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha works in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Ha earned a master's degree at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and a PhD at Duke University under Stanley Abe (attested 2016).

Junjirō Takakusu was a Buddhist studies scholar and Indologist who studied at Oxford, Leipzig, and under Max Müller. He served as professor and president at the University of Tokyo, rector at Toyo University, and founding principal of Osaka University of Foreign Studies.

Junkei Washio was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Toyo University and subsequently served as a professor at both Komazawa University and Toyo University, and taught at the Sendan-Rin School.

Junkichi Imanishi was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He was an associate professor at Hokkaido University (ca. 1967–1996) and served as Chancellor of the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (ca. 1996–2011).

Junko Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed an MA at the Australian National University and a doctorate at the University of Göttingen. She held a professorship at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2011).

Junko Minamoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed graduate studies at Ryukoku University and Otani University. She has served as a commissioned researcher at Kansai University.
